title: The reverse repo stopped being the floor in 2022
sources: RBI, Statement on Developmental and Regulatory Policies, April 2022 (SDF as floor of the LAF corridor; FRRR at 3.35 per cent retained)
RBI, Governor's Statement, 7 October 2026 (repo 5.50, SDF 5.25, MSF and Bank Rate 5.75 per cent)

quiz.q: Which facility is now the floor of the RBI's corridor?
quiz.why: Right. Since April 2022 the Standing Deposit Facility, 25 bps below repo, is the floor; the MSF is the ceiling.

script: Many notes still call the reverse repo the floor for short-term rates.

steps.text: Policy repo rate in the middle

claims.claim: In April 2022 the SDF replaced the fixed rate reverse repo (FRRR) as the floor of the LAF corridor (2022)
claims.quote: the SDF will replace the fixed rate reverse repo (FRRR) as the floor

claims.claim: The SDF is 25 bps below the repo rate (a quarter point) and absorbs liquidity without collateral; the MSF is 25 bps above repo and is the ceiling
The FRRR (3.35 per cent then) was retained in the toolkit but is no longer the corridor floor
As of 7 October 2026: policy repo rate 5.50 (5.5) per cent, SDF 5.25 per cent, MSF and Bank Rate 5.75 per cent

review_note: Primary: RBI April 2022 statement and RBI 7 October 2026 Governor's statement. Moving numbers carry 'as of October 2026' on screen and in narration; re-check after the next MPC meeting (rates change). The hook 'many notes still call the reverse repo the floor' is an editorial framing, not a sourced fact. Left out: what the MPC is, CRR/SLR, OMOs, variable-rate repo/reverse repo auctions.
